_about: Seats for /connect (lib/connect_roles.py). assign() enumerates every planner x coder x reviewer triple, drops a triple that breaks R1 to R5, and takes the lowest planner rank, then coder rank, then reviewer rank; billing class breaks ties (flat-rate subscription or membership, then free, then metered). Metered prices are USD per million tokens from the vendors' own pages, read 2026-11-11: DeepSeek's peak rate, Google's rate for prompts up to 200k tokens, xAI's list rate. max_in bounds the prompt in bytes (a byte bounds a token) and max_out is the output cap each call sends. DeepSeek v4 Pro spends its output cap on hidden reasoning before any answer: a 16,384 cap returned nothing for a 13 KB review prompt and 64,000 answered it (measured 2026-10-05), so its seats get 64,000. The per-run cap is a worst-case reservation, not expected spend: it holds one review plus the repair round's re-review at DeepSeek's worst case. The coder seat names no Codex home: lib/connect.py picks a ready subscription home from the untracked config/codex-accounts.json at admit time. The planner's fable-5.2 row is the one seat allowed transport claude-cch instead of claude-p (R2, GRIP#9272) -- it needs a working ~/.hal (or $HAL_HOME) checkout with a CCH subscription token; with neither, this seat always fails and opus-5.5 plans every run instead, visibly in the run's notes, never a crash.

dictated._about: Bounds for a HAL model the operator dictates with --planner, --coder or --reviewer (lib/connect_roles.dictate). A HAL seat is free only on a local catalogue tier; every other HAL call is metered, whatever the catalogue's paid flag or subscription tier says. A metered seat is priced from an override row under prices (USD per million tokens, both price_in and price_out above zero; max_out may override the role's bound), else from the published price lib/hal/cost_tracker.py bills; with neither, R3 refuses it, so it is never priced at zero.
